title: Choose the visual world — Yuuki Burleigh portfolio
question: The roll assigned Data-Centre Wayfinding. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Data-Centre Wayfinding
options.lineage: colo-floor signage: row/rack/U labels, aisle markings, floor-tile grid, safety-yellow
options.thesis: The portfolio is a lab floor you walk: every lab is filed at the rack and device it configured.
options.viewport: Isometric plate of one lab row; a packet runs the cable switch→router→firewall→VPN→cloud→AI; each device carries a printed label (R02-U14 SWITCH · 4 LABS) that opens its labs; name, title, 'Email me' on a big signage panel at left.
options.risk: Signage can read cold or like an airport if the labels are not set with real typographic care.

raised.raise: A running head names the span you are in (ROW A · SWITCH → FIREWALL), recomputed as you scroll.
Devices sit unlit until the packet reaches them; lit = you are here, the only warm state on the floor.
Rack-unit and port numbers are fixed tabular positions, never decoration and never invented metrics.
The isometric plate runs full-bleed across the hero and breaks across sections, never boxed in a card.

options.label: Isometric Topology Sheet
options.lineage: vendor network diagrams (isometric device stencils, link labels, legend block)
options.thesis: The site is the network diagram of your labs, drawn to engineering-sheet standard.
options.viewport: One full-width topology sheet; devices as stencils linked by labelled cables; a title block bottom-right holds name, certs, contact.
options.risk: The literal reading of the brief and where most network portfolios land; can look like a Visio export.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Packets as pure data: barcode columns and a sine lattice in black and white, the path traced through them.
options.viewport: A wall of bar-columns; the packet path is one inverted column per device; labs pulled into focus per column.
options.case: Holds audience identification (reads as data/network to engineers); loses on clarity: recruiters may not see devices or labs.
options.risk: Fights the pinned isometric device plate; strobing must stop under reduced motion.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder & Plate
options.thesis: Labs as dictionary entries, colour quarantined in plates.
options.viewport: Two-column entries with a mineral-style plate of the rack.
options.case: Recruiters don't identify with a lexicon; cream+serif is a known AI look.
options.risk: Bookish costume on a network portfolio.
options.kept: Guide words: the head names the span you are inside.

options.label: Akari Workshop
options.thesis: Labs as paper lanterns lit one at a time.
options.viewport: Glowing volumes in a dim room.
options.case: No link to network hardware; loses both axes.
options.kept: Lit = inhabited: state is light, unlit forms wait.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.case: Needs metrics the product forbids inventing.
options.kept: Fixed digit positions: numbers are tabular and real.

options.label: Itasha Vinyl Wrap
options.viewport: Illustration across panels, sponsor strip nav.
options.kept: Art scaled to break across panels, never boxed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark tech portfolio: hero, about, projects grid, certs, contact — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and title left, illustration right, CTA buttons below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tech portfolio by design.
